title: Прапорщик Задов и деньги  (Ensign Zadov and Money)

segments.t: Upstairs at Kirill Ilyich's door, Dmitry Nagiyev introduces himself and offers peace. Unfortunately, the retired officer recognizes Nagiyev from his comedic television role as Ensign Zadov and takes grave offense when Nagiyev offers him money. Listen to their exchange in Russian first.
Я к тебе правда с миром пришёл.
Я просто тебе хотел денег предложить.
Now let's go back through their conversation line by line and unpack the Russian phrasing.
'What do you want?' In Russian, the idea of 'what' flows naturally into 'need' without extra filler words. Dmitry Nagiyev answers right away.
'Hello, my name is Dmitry.' The meaning hinges on 'hello' working together with 'is called' in spoken Russian.
'Well, you look familiar to me.' The meaning hinges on 'so' working together with 'familiar' in spoken Russian.
'Wait, are you that warrant officer?' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'this' and finishing on 'warrant officer'. Dmitry Nagiyev answers right away.
'Well done, you recognized me.' Dmitry Nagiyev brings out the contrast between 'well done' and 'to recognise' in a few short words.
'I am offering you peace.' In Russian, the idea of 'I' flows naturally into 'suggest' without extra filler words.
'What kind of peace for you?' In Russian, the idea of 'what' flows naturally into 'world' without extra filler words.
'You disgraced all Russian warrant officers!' Notice how Russian expresses 'you' and 'disgraced' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
'You disgraced the entire Russian army!' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'you' before landing on 'disgraced'.
Я к тебе правда с миром пришёл.
'I truly came to you in peace.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'I' and finishing on 'arrived'.
Я просто тебе хотел денег предложить.
'I just wanted to offer you some money.' In Russian, the idea of 'I' flows naturally into 'to offer' without extra filler words.
'You decided to offer me money?' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'money' and finishing on 'to offer'. Alright, let's hear the entire conversation one more time from start to finish.
Я к тебе правда с миром пришёл.
Я просто тебе хотел денег предложить.
Offering cash to a proud retired officer who already hates Nagiyev's television character turns out to be a painful mistake. See you next time!
